context:
Follow the established TPC-DS modular pattern (not the older TPC-H single-file pattern):

Reference implementation: benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/
├── __init__.py           # Public API: get_tpcds_query(), list_tpcds_queries(), TPCDS_DATAFRAME_QUERIES
├── registry.py           # QueryRegistry("tpcds") instantiation and accessor functions
├── queries.py            # Dual-family implementations: q{N}_expression_impl + q{N}_pandas_impl
├── parameters.py         # get_parameters(query_id) for parameterized substitution
├── channel_helper.py     # Benchmark-specific helper (reusable pattern logic)
└── rollup_helper.py      # Benchmark-specific helper

For each new benchmark:
1. Study the SQL queries in benchbox/core/{benchmark}/queries.py to understand schema, join patterns, and edge cases
2. Create benchbox/core/{benchmark}/dataframe_queries/ directory following the TPC-DS structure
3. Implement expression family first (ctx.col(), ctx.lit(), ctx.get_table() pattern) - see q3_expression_impl in tpcds/queries.py
4. Implement pandas family second (string indexing, .merge(), .groupby() pattern) - see q3_pandas_impl in tpcds/queries.py
5. Register via QueryRegistry("{benchmark_id}") and wrap each pair in DataFrameQuery()
6. Set supports_dataframe: True in benchmark_registry.py BENCHMARK_METADATA
7. Write tests following tests/unit/core/tpcds/test_tpcds_dataframe_queries.py pattern
8. Validate each query against SQL results at SF=0.01

Key pattern differences per benchmark:
- Single-table benchmarks (ClickBench, H2ODB): No joins, simpler - skip helpers.py
- Star-schema (SSB): Reuse TPC-H join patterns but with different key columns
- Time-series (TSBS): Need date_trunc/time-bucket helpers
- ETL (TPC-DI, Write Primitives): Need write operation helpers (to_parquet, concat)
- Variant benchmarks (TPC-H Skew, TPC-Havoc): Maximize reuse of TPC-H impls
description:
Extend BenchBox's DataFrame execution capability to all SQL-only benchmarks.

Currently, only TPC-H (22 queries) and TPC-DS (99 queries) have DataFrame support.
This initiative will add DataFrame implementations for the remaining 16 benchmarks
(excluding only Transaction Primitives which require ACID guarantees), totaling
approximately 700+ query/operation implementations across two execution families
(expression-based and pandas-based).

Key insight: DataFrames are NOT read-only. All major DataFrame libraries support
write operations (to_parquet, write_csv, sink operations) and transformation
patterns that map directly to SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE semantics. TPC-DI
ETL operations and Write Primitives are actually IDEAL DataFrame workloads since
Pandas/Polars/PySpark are the de facto ETL tools in the Python ecosystem.

This enables users to benchmark DataFrame libraries (Polars, Pandas, PySpark,
DataFusion, Modin, cuDF, Dask) against SQL databases using a broader range of
workloads beyond the current TPC benchmarks.

NOTE: This is a large tracking TODO. After Phase 1 completes, consider splitting
Tiers 2-4 into per-tier TODOs with their own guardrails and verification.

anti_patterns.dont: add DataFrame queries without validating against SQL results
anti_patterns.instead: validate every query against SQL output at SF=0.01 before committing
anti_patterns.why: silent correctness bugs accumulate and are hard to find later

anti_patterns.dont: add benchmark-specific logic to platform adapters in benchbox/platforms/dataframe/
anti_patterns.instead: put benchmark-specific helpers in the benchmark's own dataframe_queries/helpers.py

anti_patterns.dont: copy TPC-H query implementations into other benchmarks verbatim
anti_patterns.instead: analyze the benchmark's SQL queries first and translate the logical operations
anti_patterns.why: each benchmark has different schema semantics, column names, and join patterns

anti_patterns.dont: implement all 700+ queries in a single pass
anti_patterns.instead: implement one benchmark at a time with incremental commits and validation
anti_patterns.why: review quality degrades with large changesets

anti_patterns.dont: modify DataFrameQuery, DataFrameContext, or DataFrameContextImpl classes
anti_patterns.instead: if new capabilities are needed, extend via subclass or helper functions
anti_patterns.why: that risks breaking existing TPC-H/TPC-DS implementations and all 8 platform adapters

anti_patterns.instead: new benchmarks get their own isolated dataframe_queries/ directories

deferrals.reason: ETL pipeline with mutation-heavy operations (SCD Type 2, incremental loads). Requires fundamentally different DataFrame patterns (stateful transforms, write operations) beyond read-only query model. Needs separate TODO with dedicated architecture.
INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL operations don't map to DataFrame read-query model. Would need write-operation adapter layer not currently in DataFrameContext. Needs separate TODO.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] obsolete: Verified DONE: integrate-write-primitives-dataframe-mode.yaml and dataframe-write-primitives.yaml (both Completed) already implement Write Primitives DataFrame INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL/MERGE.

deferrals.reason: 89 SQL queries (not 17 as originally estimated) need significant adaptation from multi-table TPC-DS to single-table OBT schema. The queries reference a fully denormalized table that doesn't map cleanly to existing TPC-DS DataFrame implementations. Needs separate TODO.

220 query variants exist to test SQL optimizer behavior (syntax rewriting, predicate pushdown, etc.). These test SQL engine internals, not logical query semantics - DataFrame execution bypasses SQL parsing entirely. Minimal value for DataFrame benchmarking. Needs separate evaluation if desired.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] obsolete: TPC-Havoc DataFrame impl judged 'minimal value' since it tests SQL-optimizer internals that DataFrame execution bypasses entirely; same conclusion as deferral 374.

deferrals.reason: 113 queries specifically designed to test SQL optimizer join ordering decisions. DataFrame libraries handle joins programmatically (user specifies order), making this benchmark meaningless for DataFrame evaluation. Needs separate TODO if desired.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Explicitly deemed benchmark-meaningless for DataFrame evaluation (JoinOrder tests SQL optimizer join-ordering); no open item wants it.

deferrals.reason: 136 queries are catalog-driven with different architecture (programmatic query generation from schema introspection). Many test DB-specific features (INFORMATION_SCHEMA, SHOW commands). Needs separate evaluation and likely a different implementation approach.
